label: Admissible knowability contents: C is an explicit family of world-indexed predicates
definition: C is an explicit family of world-indexed predicates. RestrictedKnowability applies only at actuality and only to C; MooreAdmissible independently requires C to contain the Moore content. GlobalRestrictedEquivalence instead requires q(w) iff possible knowledge at every world. The survivor C contains all predicates invariant under equal values of its nonconstant atom, hence contains every Boolean combination of that atom. It excludes the Moore content; no epistemic syntax adequacy theorem is claimed.
note: Analyst formulation for #1053; attribution deferred. Applicability to real knowledge and semantic antirealism remains open. See docs/notes/sep-fitch-knowability-gap-20261106.md.
